course.title: Attention Is All You Need
course.institution: Google Brain, Google Research and University of Toronto (NIPS 2017)
course.instructor: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
course.level: curious beginner; assumes vectors, dot products and the idea of a weighted average

units.title: Introduction
units.summary: Recurrent sequence models process tokens one after another, which limits parallel training on long sequences; the paper proposes the Transformer, which relies on attention alone to relate positions.

units.title: Background
units.summary: Earlier convolutional models need more operations to connect distant positions as distance grows; self-attention relates any two positions of one sequence in a constant number of steps.

units.title: Encoder and decoder stacks
units.summary: The model stacks six identical encoder layers and six decoder layers, each built from attention and feed-forward sublayers wrapped in residual connections and layer normalisation.

units.title: Scaled dot-product attention
units.summary: Each query is compared with every key by a dot product, the scores are divided by the square root of the key dimension and turned into weights by a softmax, and the output is the weighted average of the values.

units.title: Multi-head attention
units.summary: Instead of one attention function on full-width vectors, the model projects queries, keys and values into several smaller subspaces, runs attention in each head in parallel and concatenates the results.

units.title: Applications of attention in the model
units.summary: Attention is used three ways: encoder-decoder attention, encoder self-attention, and decoder self-attention with a mask that stops positions from looking at later tokens.

units.title: Position-wise feed-forward networks
units.summary: After attention, every position passes independently through the same two-layer network with a ReLU, widening from 512 to 2048 dimensions and back.

units.title: Embeddings and softmax
units.summary: Learned embeddings turn tokens into vectors, and the same weight matrix is shared between the input embeddings and the output projection before the final softmax.

units.title: Positional encoding
units.summary: Because attention ignores order, sine and cosine waves of different frequencies are added to the embeddings so the model can tell positions apart and relate relative offsets.

units.title: Why self-attention
units.summary: Compares self-attention with recurrent and convolutional layers on cost per layer, how much can run in parallel, and the longest path a signal must travel between two positions.

units.title: Training
units.summary: Describes the WMT translation data and batching, training on eight GPUs, the Adam optimiser with a warm-up learning-rate schedule, and regularisation by dropout and label smoothing.

units.title: Machine translation and model variations
units.summary: The Transformer beats earlier models on English-German and English-French translation at a fraction of the training cost, and ablations vary heads, key size, depth and dropout.

units.title: English constituency parsing
units.summary: The same architecture, with little task-specific tuning, also performs well on parsing sentences into constituency trees, showing it generalises beyond translation.

units.title: Conclusion
units.summary: Summarises the Transformer as the first sequence transduction model built entirely on attention and outlines plans to apply it to other modalities and longer inputs.
